vo_text.1: Stop throwing dead stink bait on the bottom if you want flatheads. You're catching channel cats, not river monsters.
vo_text.2: Flathead catfish aren't scavengers. They are apex solitary predators. During the day, they lock themselves deep inside heavy cover: root balls, logjams, and undercut clay banks in deep river scour holes.
vo_text.3: When the sun goes down, they leave the wood to hunt. To catch them, you must use live, struggling bait. Rig a six to eight inch live bluegill or bullhead on an eight aught circle hook with a heavy slip sinker rig.
vo_text.4: The vibrations drive them wild. When a flathead hits, let the rod load completely before locking down your drag. Their massive, bony mouth requires maximum pressure.
vo_text.5: Ditch the dead bait, target heavy wood, and hit subscribe for more trophy breakdown guides.
